content.title: About
content.content: Salsa verde is a classic Mexican sauce made from fresh tomatillos, chilies, onion, garlic, cilantro and lime. It has a bright, slightly tangy and spicy flavor that pairs perfectly with tacos, nachos, grilled meats and seafood.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Salsa verde is traditionally served cold, but it can also be gently warmed.
Tomatillos are rich in antioxidants such as vitamin C and carotenoids.
The original recipe uses only fresh cilantro, though some regions add parsley.
The heat level can range from mild to very hot depending on the type and amount of chilies used.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Low‑calorie sauce
items.content: Salsa verde is low in calories, making it a great choice for weight‑conscious diets.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Tomatillos and lime provide antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Cilantro and lime may promote digestion thanks to their natural enzymes.

items.title: Cilantro allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to cilantro.

items.title: Spiciness
items.content: Very hot salsa can cause discomfort for people with sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If salt is added, monitor the amount, especially for low‑sodium diets.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Serve salsa verde with tacos, burritos, nachos, grilled meats, fish, seafood, or use it as a marinade or salad dressing.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salsa in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. When frozen, it can last up to 2 months, though the texture may change slightly.
